newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST-Japan Nov trade surplus seen falling 28%.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Japan Nov trade surplus seen falling 28%.

text.p: Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus for November is expected to drop from last year's level, with the average of economists' forecasts being for a fall of around 28 percent to 488 billion yen.
The economists' forecasts for Japan's customs-cleared November trade surplus ranged from 443 billion yen to 590 billion yen. The surplus last November was 673.6 billion yen.

The trade figures for November are to be released on Wednesday. If the figures are in line with the forecasts, it would be the 24th consecutive month that the surplus has declined on a year-on-year basis.
Economists said continued robust car exports due to the increased competitiveness of Japanese products abroad following the weakening of the yen will help shrink Japan's trade surplus for November.
But imports, particularly of communications equipment and semiconductor products, remain on the rise, they said.
Preliminary trade figures for the first 20 days of October showed a 49.5 percent year-on-year drop in the surplus to 171.3 billion yen.
